column9: Every time Priority Override Request is arriving
column10:
.Sir,
Please consider the following scenario:
A godown has five (05) stacks with the dates of formation as under:
Stack 1/1 – 01.01.2026
Stack 1/8 – 01.01.2026
Stack 2/6 – 03.01.2026
Stack 2/4 – 04.01.2026
Stack 3/6 – 07.01.2026
The depot has 05 labour gangs, each consisting of 11 labourers, and the depot is required to issue 70 trucks on the same day.
In such circumstances, issuance has to be carried out simultaneously from all five stacks to ease operations and to optimally utilize the available labour gangs. However, the system repeatedly raises a priority override request whenever issuance is attempted from multiple stacks.
Practically, issuing large quantities by completely exhausting one stack before moving to another is not feasible, especially when handling a high number of trucks in a single day. To ensure smooth, efficient, and timely issue operations, issuance from multiple stacks simultaneously becomes unavoidable.
Therefore, it is requested that the system may be suitably modified so that issuance from multiple stacks is allowed without priority override, proportionate to the number of labour gangs available at the depot, to facilitate operational convenience and avoid unnecessary system constraints

• Export facility to Excel/PDF for official use

column9: Provision for all linked depots to receive stocks directly against a single RR number
column10:
During rake unloading at RH SCE (consignee depot FSD Senchowa), RH GUP (consignee depot: HG Balajan), etc the trucks directly dispatched to linked depots are neither weighed at Railhead LWB or at Consignee depot LWB, but are weighed only at the recipient depots due to non-availability of LWB at Railhead and the depots located in different routes. This makes rake unloading online through Annadarpan not possible. 
Hence, there should be provision for all linked depots to receive stocks directly against an RR number (not necessarily through the LWB of the consignee depot alone); However, TL report & DSR for the entire rake/RR should be generated at the consignee depot like FSD Senchowa as per the SOP. Currently, the same is being done in DOS through Offline source by creating multiple identities(Friendly Names) for same rake/RR number which is not advisable and the TL report/DSR for the entire rake/RR are not being generated at the consignee depot.

column9: Issues in Weighbridge Inspection Module – Non-Availability of Inspection Timing and Printing of Zero/Pro Weight Slips
column10:
In the Weighbridge Inspection module, two separate options are presently available, namely:
Record Weighbridge Inspection – wherein Zero Weight and Pro Weight inspections are recorded; and
Weighbridge Inspection List – wherein details of the inspections carried out can be viewed.
In this connection, the following issues have been noticed:
1) In the Weighbridge Inspection List, complete details of the inspection are not being reflected. Specifically, the timing of inspection (exact time) is not available in the detailed view, which is an essential parameter from an operational and audit perspective.
2)There is no provision for printing Zero Weight Slip and Pro Weight Slip after recording the inspection. These slips are mandatory documents for verification and record purposes prior to commencement of daily weighbridge operations.
The following enhancements are suggested for operational effectiveness and compliance:
1.	Provision may be incorporated to display inspection exact time (timestamp) in the Weighbridge Inspection List details.
2.	An option may be provided to generate and print Zero Weight Slip and Pro Weight Slip immediately after recording the inspection.
3.	The system may also allow re-printing of the slips from the Inspection List for record and audit requirements.
These modifications will strengthen transparency, ensure procedural compliance before start of operations, and improve overall usability of the module.

column9: Enabling Depot-level Modification of Variety-wise Quantity in ROs to Ensure FIFO Compliance
column10:
It is submitted that Release Orders are generally created at the level of the Divisional Office wherein, for Rice, the variety Parboiled Common and for Wheat, FAQ are selected by default while generating the Release Orders.

Subsequently, depots receive stocks of different varieties, such as Grade-A Rice and URS Wheat, against later receipts. In such cases, the concerned depot submits a request in the module for conversion of variety so as to facilitate issuance of stocks accordingly.

However, the existing system provision allows conversion of variety-wise quantity only once against the Release Order. Thereafter, depots are unable to modify the variety-wise breakup despite continuous receipt of stocks of different crop years and varieties. Since stocks received later often attain priority for issuance under FIFO principles, depots are frequently required to realign the variety-wise quantities of the Release Orders to ensure compliance with FIFO and proper stock rotation.

In the absence of a repeat modification facility, depots face operational difficulty in issuing stocks strictly on FIFO basis, particularly when multiple varieties and crop years are held simultaneously.

In view of the above, it is requested that necessary system provisioning may kindly be made in Anna Darpan to enable depots to modify / re-adjust the variety-wise quantities in Release Orders more than once, as per stock availability and FIFO requirement. This will facilitate smooth issuance operations and ensure adherence to prescribed stock rotation norms.

column9: PORTAL LOGOUT ISSUE
column10:
Dear IT टीम,
निवेदन है कि Anna Darpan Portal पर कार्य करते समय एक गंभीर तकनीकी समस्या का सामना करना पड़ रहा है। पोर्टल पर काम के दौरान अचानक ऑटोमेटिक लॉगआउट हो जाता है, जिससे उपयोगकर्ता का चल रहा कार्य बाधित हो जाता है और पूरा कार्य पुनः प्रारंभ करना पड़ता है। इससे समय की हानि होती है तथा कार्य की उत्पादकता प्रभावित होती है।
इस समस्या के समाधान हेतु निम्नलिखित सुझाव प्रस्तुत किए जाते हैं:
1.	Session Timeout अवधि बढ़ाई जाए - वर्तमान सेशन टाइमआउट बहुत कम प्रतीत होता है। इसे कम से कम 30–60 मिनट तक बढ़ाया जाए, विशेषकर डेटा एंट्री या रिपोर्टिंग मॉड्यूल में।
2.	Auto Save Feature लागू किया जाए - पोर्टल में ऑटो-सेव फीचर जोड़ा जाए ताकि लॉगआउट या नेटवर्क समस्या की स्थिति में डेटा सुरक्षित रहे।
3.	Session Expiry Warning Message - दिया जाए लॉगआउट से पहले पॉप-अप चेतावनी दी जाए ताकि उपयोगकर्ता सेशन रिन्यू कर सके।
4.	Server Stability और Load Testing किया जाए - सर्वर लोड या नेटवर्क लेटेंसी के कारण सेशन ड्रॉप हो सकता है, अतः सर्वर पर लोड टेस्टिंग और परफॉर्मेंस ऑप्टिमाइजेशन किया जाए।
5.	Client Activity Detection लागू किया जाए - यदि उपयोगकर्ता पोर्टल पर सक्रिय है (डेटा भर रहा है या क्लिक कर रहा है), तो सेशन ऑटो एक्सपायर न हो।
6.	Network Resilience Improvement - कमजोर इंटरनेट कनेक्शन की स्थिति में सेशन को बनाए रखने हेतु री-कनेक्शन मैकेनिज्म लागू किया जाए।

उपरोक्त सुधारों से पोर्टल की उपयोगिता एवं कार्य दक्षता में उल्लेखनीय वृद्धि होगी।
कृपया आवश्यक तकनीकी सुधार करने की कृपा करें।
धन्यवाद।

This modification is necessary to ensure accurate record maintenance and data consistency between Inspection and Curative modules.

column9: Request for Technical Rectification of Rice Commodity Classification in AnnaDarpan Portal at FSD Wardha........Reg
column10:
Respected Sir/Madam,

     This is to bring to your kind notice that the total stock quantity reflected in the DOS and AnnaDarpan portal is matching correctly. However, a discrepancy has been observed in the classification of rice commodity. In the DOS system, the entire rice stock of FSD Wardha is shown under the head “Raw Rice”, while in actual physical terms, the complete stock consists only of FRK Raw Rice. The DOS system was also considering the stock as FRK Raw Rice in practice. However, in the AnnaDarpan portal, the same stock is being displayed under two different categories, namely: 1)Raw Rice , 2)FRK Raw Rice . Since FSD Wardha is holding only FRK Raw Rice, this incorrect bifurcation may lead to inconsistencies in future transactions and may create problems during stock issuance and reconciliation. 
     In view of the above, you are kindly requested to arrange for the necessary technical correction in the AnnaDarpan portal so that the entire rice stock of FSD Wardha is reflected only under the category “FRK Raw Rice”, in order to avoid any discrepancies in future.

column9: Regarding Issuance of Release Order
column10: In view of the subject cited above, it is suggested that suitable system-level enhancements may be considered in the AnnaDarpan portal to facilitate block-wise creation of Release Orders (ROs) as required by the State Agencies. Further, in several cases, a single block is required to be bifurcated or split into two or more depots while generating ROs for State Agencies; however, such a provision is presently not available in AnnaDarpan, which restricts operational flexibility. Additionally, as ROs are presently required to be fed simultaneously on both DoS and AnnaDarpan portals, the process becomes time-consuming and leads to duplication of work; therefore, integration or auto-synchronization between the two systems may be explored to streamline operations. Moreover, a facility may be incorporated in AnnaDarpan for system-generated sharing of the RO with the concerned stakeholders through email or portal-based access, ensuring transparency, timely communication, and ease of compliance.

column9: Issue in Procurement module
column10:
With reference to the subject mentioned above, it is hereby highlighted that the CMR receipt operations under KMS 2025-26 have commenced at depots under this office. Consequently, during the parallel implementation of the DOS and Anna Darpan portals, in accordance with the received guidelines, the following issues have been identified concerning the procurement module:

1. The Anna Darpan portal enables millers to select a stack for CMR lots under their login credentials. However, in previous seasons, exemptions were granted for miller-specific CMR stacking, and approval was given for agency-specific TA stacking. However, till date no communication regarding approval for agency specific TA stacking for KMS 2025-26 is received. Nonetheless, the Anna Darpan portal does not permit CMR lots from different millers to be combined into a single stack if the delivery was made by another miller, even if the paddy was procured from the same agency.
2. Furthermore, it is important to note that this office has completed all necessary formalities on the WINGS portal for the receipt of the CMR, including capturing the geocoordinates of the mills, generating the distance and least-cost matrix, and performing load balancing. However, the data from the WINGS portal is yet to be migrated to the Anna Darpan portal. Consequently, all the procedures previously carried out on the WINGS portal must be repeated on the Anna Darpan portal.
Therefore, it is requested to kindly provide necessary direction/guidelines regarding acceptance of CMR in Anna Darpan portal so that CMR operations can be performed parallelly at DOS and Anna Darpan portal

column9: Bifurcation of Allotted qty. to centers
column10: In the Anna Darpan Portal, movements are created by the Regional Office by defining the source as a center such as Hoshiarpur, which comprises multiple depots including FSD, CWC, PSWC, Markfed, etc. However, at the time of adding the movement, the entire allocation is mapped only against FSD instead of the center as a whole, due to which the allocated quantity is reflected only in the movement list of FSD, while other depots under the same center are unable to view the allocation in their respective logins and are consequently unable to generate tokens despite availability of stock. In order to address this limitation, it is suggested that either the allocation may be made at the center level so that a common allocation is reflected across all depots linked to the center, or alternatively, an enabling provision may be made in the portal whereby FSD is given the option to further distribute the allotted quantity among other depots of the same center on priority basis, so that all concerned depots can generate tokens as per their allocated share and ensure smooth, flexible and timely movement of foodgrains.
column47: Movements have to be created between source and destination depots, then only it will allow to generate tokens.

column9: Issues/suggestions related to Contract Module
column10:
Issues while adding contractor:
1. we are unable to select the state other than Telangana. Whereas contractor may belong to any state other than Telangana , hence it would be better to have an option to select any state.
2. (a) MSE category has been a mandatory option whereas all the contractors may not come under MSE category , some might be under medium category also.
    (b) In MSE category options are available for only few categories like SC/ST/Women and there are no options for OBC/General category.
3. ESIC number is a mandatory option and it is only accepting the new format (14 digit) numbers only whereas few contractors having ESIC numbers in old format which is an alpha-numeric code and may not be      14 characters. Hence , it would be better to remove ESIC as a mandatory option and access may be given to enter number in either of the formats.
4. FSSAI license is a mandatory option without which we are unable to add contractor but the contractors may or may not have FSSAI license. It would be better to remove it as a mandatory option.
5. As the rate quoted by the contractors for Handling and Transport contract is inclusive of GST, at present GST is not applicable for Handling and transportation services for warehousing activities in FCI. Hence the field for GST may not be mandatory.
6. MICR is a mandatory option. It can be an aditional option but need not be mandatory.

Suggestions for editing contractor
1. While editing contractor details only few options are available , need edit options for all the fields.
2. In addition to view and edit , deleting of the contractor option need to be added. 

Other Suggestions
1.List of transport contracts are available/visible with  transporter name or district name. Instead of tender number and district name fields , from depot and  to depot name need to be inserted.
2.While editing transport contract , option for editing is limited to few fields. Hence option for editing may be given to all fields. Few fields which were actually not mandatory while creating contract, are made mandatory during editing and this mandatory option may be removed at the time of editing.  
3.While creating conracts (Handling/Transportation/Both/Multimodal) the information/details of Security amount , Bank Guarante are mandatory at present. Whereas in Telangana Region, the H&T contracts of hired depots will be awarded by their respective agencies (SWC/CWC). Hence , mandatory option may be removed which enables creating of contracts easy.
4. In handling and transportation contract list only approved and pending lists are displayed. Approved/Pending/Rejected contract list for all the contracts should be displayed.
5.At present contracts are searchable and visible only with tender numbers which is very difficult to identify the perticular tender. Search/displaying of contracts with center name would be better.
6. Provision for debarrment : Provision for maintaining Nation wide DEBARMENT LIST/TERMINATION LIST along with details of period, which enables all offices across nation to cross check and award contract to L1 party

column9: Request to modify ICCS Team Assignment logic from 'Issue Point-specific' to 'Rake-specific'
column10: Request for functional update regarding the assignment of ICCS teams within the Anna Darpan Portal. Under the current system configuration, users are required to  assign an ICCS team for every individual issue point associated with a loading operation. This process is highly repetitive and inefficient because, in standard operational practice, a single team is responsible for the entire rake regardless of how many issue points are involved. The system logic should be modified to make ICCS team assignment rake-specific rather than issue point-specific. We propose that the portal allow for a single team assignment at the Rake/Indent level, which would then automatically cascade or apply to all associated issue points for that specific loading task.

column9: Issue in MBR Creation – Depot Dropdown Not Appearing When “Centre” Option Selected
column10:
While creating Movement by Road (MBR) in the Anna Darpan portal, during allocation entry, if the option “Is Centre – Yes” is selected, the Source Depot dropdown does not display the list of depots. The dropdown remains blank/loading and no depot options appear for selection.This is creating difficulty in proceeding further with MBR creation.
Suggestion for System Improvement: Since allocation is finalized centre-wise at Regional Office (RO) level, provision of “Centre” selection alone is sufficient at RO level. Therefore, it is suggested that: The mandatory depot selection option at Regional level may be removed, OR Depot selection provision may be shifted to Divisional Office level, where depots can be selected based on stock priority. At RO level, simple provision to select Centre and Division should be adequate for allocation purposes.This modification will streamline the MBR creation process and align it with the existing allocation workflow.

column9: Feedback on inadequacy of Mandtory reports for monitoring and review of essential depot operations
column10:
In the Storage module, there is no provision for generation of Commodity-wise and Crop Year-wise Opening Balance, Inflow and Outflow statements between two dates, for a month or for a specific date, for a single depot, multiple depots or all depots under a Divisional Office, Regional Office or Zonal Office. These statements, which include details of receipts, issues, storage gain, storage loss and other adjustments, are already available in IRRS and are critical for reviewing stock movement and operational efficiency. Provision of such reports in Anna Darpan would greatly ease retrieval of information from the data already entered in the system.

Further, there is no provision for generation of a comprehensive Stock Account for a single depot, multiple depots or all depots at Divisional, Regional, Zonal or Headquarters level between two dates or for a month. Such a report should necessarily provide Commodity-wise and Crop Year-wise details of Opening Balance, Total Receipts segregated by rake, road movement and CMR, Total Issue, Total Dispatch, Storage Gain, Physical Verification Gain, Storage Loss, Physical Verification Loss and Closing Balance. This Stock Account is extremely important for monthly review and reconciliation of depot operations and therefore needs to be provisioned in the Anna Darpan portal.

It is also observed that there is no provision for generating a Commodity-wise stock position report indicating percentage utilization for a single depot, multiple depots or all depots under Divisional, Regional, Zonal Office or Headquarters on a date-wise basis, for a specific date, a month or a defined period. Such a report should also indicate storage capacity, turnover quantity, i.e. total quantities received and issued during the period, and average stock held during the period, to enable meaningful review of capacity utilization and operationalization of depots.

Additionally, there is no provision for generation of a Gunny Statement for a single depot, multiple depots or all depots under Divisional, Regional, Zonal Office or Headquarters on date-wise, period-wise or month-wise basis. column9: Request for Enabling Asset Stock Update / Store Option in AnnaDarpan Portal for Chemical Stock Management
column10:
It is submitted that earlier, in the DOS portal, the “Store” option was available in both the Manager (Depot) and Manager (QC) user IDs. Through this option, functionalities such as asset type management, asset movement, and updation/editing of chemical stocks were accessible, enabling chemicals to be added or updated as per operational requirements.

At present, the said asset stock update facility is not available in either of the above user IDs in the new AnnaDarpan Portal. As a result, while entering data in the Prophylactic Treatment module, the following system-generated error message is appearing:
“Delta Metharin_Powder stock is not found. Please update the stock in Asset Update Stock Page.”

However, since the Asset Update Stock Page option itself is not visible or accessible in the AnnaDarpan Portal, it is not possible to update or add the chemical stock in the system, despite the physical availability of the chemical at the depot.

In view of the above, it is requested that the Asset Stock Update / Store option may kindly be enabled in the Manager (Depot) and Manager (QC) user IDs in the AnnaDarpan Portal, so that chemical stocks such as Deltamethrin can be duly updated in the portal and treatment entries may be carried out without system-related errors.

The matter is submitted for your kind consideration and necessary action, please.

column9: Splitting of variety of commodity during Dispatch
column10:
Splitting of variety (one-time) is available in Issue operations through Release Order. Similar provision is not provided in Dispatch operations. The one-time provision is also not sufficient since there are operational issues like RO extension, FIFO, Shortfall of approved variety of commodity etc.
Hence, the provision for change of variety should be given to the Depot or creation of MBR should be done only commodity wise and not variety wise.

column9: Issues in Weighbridge Inspection Module – Non-Availability of Inspection Timing and Printing of Zero/Pro Weight Slips
column10:
In the Weighbridge Inspection module, two separate options are presently available, namely:
Record Weighbridge Inspection – wherein Zero Weight and Pro Weight inspections are recorded; and
Weighbridge Inspection List – wherein details of the inspections carried out can be viewed.
In this connection, the following issues have been noticed:
1) In the Weighbridge Inspection List, complete details of the inspection are not being reflected. Specifically, the timing of inspection (exact time) is not available in the detailed view, which is an essential parameter from an operational and audit perspective.
2)There is no provision for printing Zero Weight Slip and Pro Weight Slip after recording the inspection. These slips are mandatory documents for verification and record purposes prior to commencement of daily weighbridge operations.
The following enhancements are suggested for operational effectiveness and compliance:
1.	Provision may be incorporated to display inspection exact time (timestamp) in the Weighbridge Inspection List details.
2.	An option may be provided to generate and print Zero Weight Slip and Pro Weight Slip immediately after recording the inspection.
3.	The system may also allow re-printing of the slips from the Inspection List for record and audit requirements.
These modifications will strengthen transparency, ensure procedural compliance before start of operations, and improve overall usability of the module.

column9: assigning of test wagon unlike DEPOT ONLINE SYSTEM.
column10: In divisional office manmad two depot comes under the same premises i.e FSD MANMAD and FSD ANKAI and RAKES usually places in both depots like 10 wagons get placed in FSD ANKAI and 32 wagons In FSD MANMAD. To start early work of RAKES we usually place 42 wagons IN FSD MANMAD and when we come to know the particulars of the wagons which places in the FSD ANKAI,we used to mark those wagons as missing wagons in the movement created for 42 wagons . now wih the 10 missing wagons we create another movement plan for FSD ANKAI .Thus we have 32 wagons in FSD MANMAD and 10 wagons in FSD ANKAI And during assigning of test wagons,DOS ask for 3 wagons as the test wagons as only 32 wagons left after missing those 10 wagons .But in ANNA DARPAN,if we creates movement plan of 42 wagons and mark 10 wagons as missing wagons even after that ANNA DARPAN ask for the test wagons according to the original movement created i.e according to 42 wagons it ask for 4 wagons as the test wagon.

column10:

In this regard, it is to inform that such a message normally appears in DOS only when a wagon has been completely unloaded and DOS does not allow consumption of more than 50 bags.

However, in the present case, not a single wagon has been unloaded in Anna Darpan, and the popping up of such an alert at this stage is surprising and is restricting further transaction.

The matter is brought to your kind notice for necessary examination and early resolution so that direct movement operation from Railhead can be carried out smoothly.

column9: Data calculation issue in Curative treatment fumigation
column10:
Please refer to the attached screenshot.

In this regard, we would like to inform you that for normal stack fumigation, the standard practice is to use 3 units (tablets) of Aluminium Phosphide per 1 MT of foodgrains.
Each tablet weighs 3 grams.

Standard practice followed:

For 1 MT we use 3 tablets = 9 grams

For example, for 100 MT of foodgrain stacks, 300 tablets (units) are used, i.e., 900 grams.

For calculation purposes, the weight in MT is rounded off using the standard rounding method prior to determining tablet quantity: The Aluminium Phosphide requirement is then calculated based on the rounded MT value.

Issue Observed:
At present, the system multiplies the exact quintal value by 9, which results in fractional values and does not align with the above-mentioned standard rounding practice.

Kindly do the necessary modification to Apply the standard rounding logic to the MT weight, and

Calculate Aluminium Phosphide tablets at the rate of 3 tablets (9 grams) per MT based on the rounded value, thereby avoiding fractional quantities.

column9: Problem in Editing of ICCS wagons (10% wagons) in a rake movement
column10:
In the rake of 58 wagons received at FSD NRPA from Ex-Moga on 04.02.2026, as per ICCS norms, 10% wagons (i.e. 6 wagons) were required to be selected for ICCS at the initial stage. Accordingly, 6 wagons were selected, and ICCS transaction in one wagon was completed successfully. Subsequently, for ease of unloading operations, the ICCS team decided to alter the ICCS wagon selection by replacing one of the previously selected ICCS wagons with another non-ICCS wagon. However, after completion of ICCS transaction in one wagon, that wagon disappeared from the editable wagon list in the Anna Darpan’s Edit Control/Test wagon section. As a result, only 5 ICCS wagons were visible under the Edit Control/Test Wagon section. While attempting to replace one of these 5 wagons with another wagon, the system triggered a pop-up message stating that at least 6 wagons (10% of 58 wagons) must be selected. Although one ICCS wagon had already been transacted and completed, the system did not count the completed ICCS wagon towards the mandatory 10% requirement.Since only 5 wagons were appearing in the list and the completed ICCS wagon was counted under the selected ICCS list of wagons, the system did not allow saving of the edited control wagon, thereby preventing replacement of the selected wagon.
This issue occurred due to a system limitation, wherein the completed ICCS wagon is excluded from the wagon list but not counted towards the required 10% ICCS wagon count, resulting in a validation error.

In the rake of 58 wagons received at FSD NRPA from Ex-Moga on 04.02.2026, as per ICCS norms, 10% wagons (i.e. 6 wagons) were required to be selected for ICCS at the initial stage. Accordingly, 6 wagons were selected, and ICCS transaction in one wagon was completed successfully. Subsequently, for ease of unloading operations, the ICCS team decided to alter the ICCS wagon selection by replacing one of the previously selected ICCS wagons with another non-ICCS wagon. However, after completion of ICCS transaction in one wagon, that wagon disappeared from the editable wagon list in the Anna Darpan’s Edit Control/Test wagon section. As a result, only 5 ICCS wagons were visible under the Edit Control/Test Wagon section. While attempting to replace one of these 5 wagons with another wagon, the system triggered a pop-up message stating that at least 6 wagons (10% of 58 wagons) must be selected. Although one ICCS wagon had already been transacted and completed, the system did not count the completed ICCS wagon towards the mandatory 10% requirement.Since only 5 wagons were appearing in the list and the completed ICCS wagon was counted under the selected ICCS list of wagons, the system did not allow saving of the edited control wagon, thereby preventing replacement of the selected wagon.
This issue occurred due to a system limitation, wherein the completed ICCS wagon is excluded from the wagon list but not counted towards the required 10% ICCS wagon count, resulting in a validation error.

column9: Regarding modifcation of data as in wings vs Annadarpan
column10:
Initial entry
o	The miller enters lot number details in Wings.
o	This data is auto-fetched once by the AnnaDarpan portal.
IF, Error in initial entry
o	If the miller’s first entry in Wings is wrong (stack no., format, etc.),
o	And later the FCI staff corrects the data in Wings,
Problem
o	AnnaDarpan does NOT re-fetch or update the corrected data.
o	It continues to display only the initial (wrong) data.
No manual correction allowed in Anndarpan.
o	The auto-fetched data in AnnaDarpan is locked.
o	Users cannot modify or overwrite the stack details in AnnaDarpan.
➡ Result: Even after correction in Wings, the error remains permanently reflected in AnnaDarpan, causing stack mismatch.

Moreover while Conducting gunny operation Mini -11 is not showing in ANNA DARPAN. It will be very much convenient if the gunny stock of all the Mini Sheds can be operated from the end of one custodian. You are therefore requested to resolve the issue as early as possible so that the pending operation of Gunny can be completed on Anna Darpan timely.

1.	Centralized Custodian Access: Enable a Master Custodian" or "Common Pool" configuration for all Mini Sheds (04–11). This would allow a single user to draw gunny from a collective stock regardless of which specific shed the grain is being moved into.

column9: Discrepancy in Display and Reporting of Palla Bags in Annadarpan System Compared to DOS
column10: While adding palla to the stack, the palla bag is displayed separately in the Annadarpan system, whereas in the DOS system it correctly appears under stock position for issue. This separation creates difficulty during wagon loading, as it becomes challenging to identify and load the correct bags into the truck. Additionally, the report does not reflect the added palla bag in the total count. For example, if the total stock is 1160 bags and 1 palla bag is taken from the store, the report should show 1161 bags; however, it continues to display 1160 bags, and the palla bag is not included. It would be preferable for the system to display the total in the same manner as DOS, allowing proper tallying with the stack ledger.

column9: Incorrect Depot and shed capacity iro FCI, FSD Hojai
column10:
It is submitted that the capacity reflected in ANNA Darpan is derived from the sum of individual stack capacities, which defines the shed capacity, and the total depot capacity is the sum of all shed capacities. However, based on verification of actual stack-wise data, the following detailed calculation is submitted for kind perusal:

Shed-wise Capacity Calculation (Based on Primary Stacks Only)
Shed – 1

87 MT × 40 stacks = 3,480 MT

116 MT × 20 stacks = 2,320 MT

145 MT × 3 stacks = 435 MT

Total Primary Stacks: 63
Total Shed-1 Capacity: 6,235 MT

Shed – 2

174 MT × 36 stacks = 6,264 MT

Total Primary Stacks: 36
Total Shed-2 Capacity: 6,264 MT

Shed – 3

174 MT × 36 stacks = 6,264 MT

116 MT × 8 stacks = 928 MT

145 MT × 2 stacks = 290 MT

100 MT × 1 stack = 100 MT

Total Primary Stacks: 47
Total Shed-3 Capacity: 7,582 MT

Total Depot Capacity (Based on Primary Stacks)

Shed-1 : 6,235 MT

Shed-2 : 6,264 MT

Shed-3 : 7,582 MT

Total Depot Capacity = 20,081 MT

Observation in ANNA Darpan

Total of shed capacities as per calculation: 20,081 MT

Capacity shown on ANNA Darpan Home Page: 20,531 MT 

Shed-wise capacities are also mismatched: Shed–I actual capacity is 6,235 MT but Anna Darpan shows 6,335 MT, and Shed–III actual capacity is 7,582 MT but Anna Darpan shows 7,632 MT.

Thus, a difference of 450 MT is observed.

On further scrutiny, it has been noticed that in Shed-1, ANNA Darpan has included secondary stack capacity while calculating shed capacity, which ideally should not be considered. As per norms, shed capacity should be computed strictly based on primary stacks only.

The inclusion of secondary stack capacity appears to be the reason for the excess capacity reflected on the ANNA Darpan Home Page.

The above is submitted for kind information and necessary corrective action, please.

column9: Allocation Period only one option available for selection
column10: For some schemes like WBNP and SAG under OWS which have quarterly allocation period, which typically would have been Jan 2026-Mar 2026, for which incidentally there exists an allocation period as Dec 2025- March 2026, for which it can be assumed that the allocation period had been provided to the HQ beforehand and therefore that is the only option. However, there are Schemes like OMSS(D) which is for the issue of Excess wheat with FCI, therefore we do not know how long this period will be, but we provide allocation period RO-wise, which in case of OMSS(D) which takes place through weekly E-Auctions, the allocaton period is 15 days for such RO, extendible by 3 days by the DM. Therefore, it is requested to either provide option to put allocation period for such cases explicitly or HQ may be requested to issue a guideline to take this period Dec 2025- March 2026 as allocation period for all ROs issued under OMSS(D).
column47: This features is implemented based on FCI comments. If changes required please raise a mail from region or HQ offices requesting this feature.

column9: Request for Enabling Asset Stock Update / Store Option in AnnaDarpan Portal for Chemical Stock Management
column10:
It is submitted that earlier, in the DOS portal, the “Store” option was available in both the Manager (Depot) and Manager (QC) user IDs. Through this option, functionalities such as asset type management, asset movement, and updation/editing of chemical stocks were accessible, enabling chemicals to be added or updated as per operational requirements.

At present, the said asset stock update facility is not available in either of the above user IDs in the new AnnaDarpan Portal. As a result, while entering data in the Prophylactic Treatment module, the following system-generated error message is appearing:
“Delta Metharin_Powder stock is not found. Please update the stock in Asset Update Stock Page.”

However, since the Asset Update Stock Page option itself is not visible or accessible in the AnnaDarpan Portal, it is not possible to update or add the chemical stock in the system, despite the physical availability of the chemical at the depot.

In view of the above, it is requested that the Asset Stock Update / Store option may kindly be enabled in the Manager (Depot) and Manager (QC) user IDs in the AnnaDarpan Portal, so that chemical stocks such as Deltamethrin can be duly updated in the portal and treatment entries may be carried out without system-related errors.

The matter is submitted for your kind consideration and necessary action, please.

We request you to kindly look into this matter on priority and provide a suitable resolution before it live in AD at the earliest.

column9: Non-Availability of Complete Data in Weighbridge Report – Requirement of Dedicated Weighbridge Register Similar to DOS
column10:
At present there is no provision for a Weighbridge Register in Anna Darpan similar to the one available in DOS.
In DOS, the Weighbridge Register provides a comprehensive record of each transaction containing the following essential details:
Token No., Gate Pass No., Truck chit No., Source of Receipt, Commodity & Variety, Truck No., No. of Bags, Gross Weight of Truck (Qtls), Tare Weight of Truck (Qtls), Gross Weight of Food Grain (Qtls), Tare Weight of Gunnies (Kgs), Net Weight of Food Grain (Qtls), and Net Weight of Loose Grain (Qtls)
However, in Anna Darpan, only a Weighment List option is available, and it does not capture or display all the above critical fields in a single consolidated format. Due to this limitation, it becomes difficult to:
1.	Maintain a complete and systematic weighment record.
2.	Cross-verify weighment-related data during day to day operatio, audit and inspection.
3.	Generate comprehensive reports for operational and reconciliation purposes.
4.	Ensure transparency and traceability of receipt and dispatch operations.
A dedicated Weighbridge Register module may kindly be incorporated in Anna Darpan on the lines of DOS, capturing all relevant transactional parameters in a single structured register format with print and export facility.
This will greatly enhance operational efficiency, record maintenance, and audit compliance.

column9: Curative treatment -standard Calculation in Kgs or Units -Reg
column10: In curative treatment, in Annadarpan each stack upto Kgs/grams has been taken for Aluminium Phosphide calculation (eg for 1A01 :157.781980 Mts*9 =1420.037820 Kgs. Manually in Registers, the weight is rounded off to Metric tonnes for Aluminium Phosphide Calculation (eg 158 *9 =1.422 Kgs). In Depotonline standard calculation for Aluminium phosphide is 3Units/Mts. In Annadarpan, the standard calculation for Aluminium phosphide is 9Units/Mts.Hence either the standard calculation may be taken as rounded figures in Kgs *9 to match the manual records or in units as in DOS .

column9: Suggestions for Modification in ICCS Team Creation and Assignment Module in Anna Darpan
column10:
In connection with the ICCS Team creation and rake assignment process in Anna Darpan, the following operational difficulties and suggestions are submitted for consideration and necessary modification in the system:
1.	Team Creation Period:
ICCS teams should be allowed to be created on a Monthly / Quarterly / Between Two Dates basis, Railhead-wise.
2.	Display of ICCS Team Members:
At present, while creating the ICCS Team the system shows Name, Contact Number, and Email ID. For better identification and operational clarity, the display format may be modified to show Name, Designation, and Place of Posting instead.
For example: Rakesh Kumar, AG-I (Depot), DO Hubballi.
This modification will enable easy identification of the official assigned to ICCS and avoid confusion, especially when multiple officers have similar names.
3.	ICCS Team Composition:
At present, ICCS teams can be created monthly or quarterly with multiple members; however, only three members actually attend ICCS operations. The system may therefore provide an option to specifically select the three members who are attending a particular rake in the particular Railhead.
4.	Default Team Assignment:
A default ICCS team consisting of three members may be auto-assigned upon placement of the rake. In case of any change, the Manager (Movement) may be provided with the authority to modify the team members from a predefined list (e.g., a panel of six approved members) for a particular rake from the Railhead Wise ICCS Team List.
5.	Temporary ICCS Provision:
An option may also be provided to create a temporary ICCS team in case of emergency for a specific rake.
6.	Rake Selection Process:
While assigning ICCS:
•	The Receipt Railhead should be selected first.
•	RR Number of all rakes en route to the destination railhead should be displayed.
•	The Manager (Movement) should have the option to select the desired rake before assigning the ICCS team.
The above modifications will improve operational clarity, reduce errors, enhance accountability, and streamline ICCS assignment in Anna Darpan.
It is requested to kindly examine the above suggestions and consider necessary system enhancements at the earliest.

column9: Suggestions for Modification in ICCS Team Creation and Assignment Module in Anna Darpan
column10:
In connection with the ICCS Team creation and rake assignment process in Anna Darpan, the following operational difficulties and suggestions are submitted for consideration and necessary modification in the system:
1.	Team Creation Period:
ICCS teams should be allowed to be created on a Monthly / Quarterly / Between Two Dates basis, Railhead-wise.
2.	Display of ICCS Team Members:
At present, while creating the ICCS Team the system shows Name, Contact Number, and Email ID. For better identification and operational clarity, the display format may be modified to show Name, Designation, and Place of Posting instead.
For example: Rakesh Kumar, AG-I (Depot), DO Hubballi.
This modification will enable easy identification of the official assigned to ICCS and avoid confusion, especially when multiple officers have similar names.
3.	ICCS Team Composition:
At present, ICCS teams can be created monthly or quarterly with multiple members; however, only three members actually attend ICCS operations. The system may therefore provide an option to specifically select the three members who are attending a particular rake in the particular Railhead.
4.	Default Team Assignment:
A default ICCS team consisting of three members may be auto-assigned upon placement of the rake. In case of any change, the Manager (Movement) may be provided with the authority to modify the team members from a predefined list (e.g., a panel of six approved members) for a particular rake from the Railhead Wise ICCS Team List.
5.	Temporary ICCS Provision:
An option may also be provided to create a temporary ICCS team in case of emergency for a specific rake.
6.	Rake Selection Process:
While assigning ICCS:
•	The Receipt Railhead should be selected first.
•	RR Number of all rakes en route to the destination railhead should be displayed.
•	The Manager (Movement) should have the option to select the desired rake before assigning the ICCS team.
The above modifications will improve operational clarity, reduce errors, enhance accountability, and streamline ICCS assignment in Anna Darpan.
It is requested to kindly examine the above suggestions and consider necessary system enhancements at the earliest.

column9: Regarding correction of stack number in AnnaDarpan
column10:
•	In Wings, stack numbers are entered as:
o	1A1, 1A2, 1A3 …
•	When the same data is auto-fetched into the AnnaDarpan portal, it appears as:
o	1A01, 1A02, 1A03 …
•	Because of this format difference, AnnaDarpan shows the error:
“This may be due to stack in issue status or a stack name mismatch”
•	When you try to edit or correct the stack number in AnnaDarpan, it does not allow the change.

column9: Unable to do MIX BAG operation in truck.
column10:
During issue transaction, SBT 580 bags are loaded alongwith HDPE madeup bags, in DOS, there is a provision to do MIX BAG operation in which we can clearly add the number of SBT 580 bags loaded alongwith number of HDPE madeup bags in a particular truck. Weight of  each bag of SBT 580 is 580 grams while weight of each bag of HDPE is 135 garms.During outweight the weight of these bags get automatically calculated by DOS and the net weight is arrived by subtracting the weight of these bags according to the number in which they are loaded in a particular truck and the tare weight. But in Anna Darpan weight of only SBT 580 is considered and there is no option to add the number of HDPE bags loaded. 
For example,
Total bags loaded = 200 bags
Suppose 180 SBT and 20 HDPE bags are loaded in a truck
In DOS (Correct – Separate Calculation)
SBT weight:180×0.58=104.4 kg
HDPE weight:20×0.135=2.7kg
Total bag weight deducted in DOS:104.4+2.7=107.1kg

In Anna Darpan (All 200 considered as SBT)
200×0.58=116kg
Total bag weight deducted = 116 kg

Difference is 116−107.1=8.9 kg
So, Anna Darpan deducts 8.9 kg more than actual because it treats all 200 bags as SBT instead of separating 20 HDPE bags, which is a loss for the depot.

So, you are requested to add the provision of MIX BAG in truck similar to DOS, so that we can do real time transaction smoothly. For your reference, screenshot of DOS is attached.

column9: Creation of Provision for scheme wise bulk approval of RO extension
column10:
1.	In the present module of Anna Darpan with respect to commodity wise extension to be given by the GM(R) for lifting of foodgrain in the 75 revenue districts under various scheme, individual Release Order are being shown for granting extension. 	It is therefore, suggested that provision for scheme wise bulk approval of RO extension raised on Anna Darpan Portal may be created for the GM(R) ID for facilitating grant of extension in bulk instead of single-single approvals for a large number of release order requiring extension.

column9: Release order validity extension at RO level
column10: If lifting under NFSA is not completed within the prescribed validity period, the first extension of 15 days is granted by the Regional Office. As per the established practice, this 15-day extension is counted from the date of issue of the extension letter, and not from the date of expiry of the original validity period. However, in Anna Darpan it has been observed that when the first 15-day extension is granted by the Regional Office, the system calculates the extended validity from the previous closing date of the Release Order instead of the date of issue of the extension letter. Presently, lifting of the NFSA February 2026 quota could not be completed in this division. The Regional Office granted the first extension of 15 days on 12.02.2026, which has extended validity up to 26.02.2026. However, when the “Extend Validity” option was exercised in Anna Darpan for the concerned Release Order, the system extended validity only up to 15.02.2026. This is inconsistent with the actual extension order issued by the Regional Office. Further, unlike the option available in DOS, there is currently no provision in Anna Darpan to manually edit or correct the validity end date of the Release Order. Due to this discrepancy, issue operations in Anna Darpan have been adversely affected as the validity period has prematurely lapsed again. In view of the above, it is requested that necessary modifications may kindly be made in Anna Darpan so that validity extensions are calculated from the date of issue of the extension order rather than from the previous closing date. This is essential for proper compliance with the prescribed rules governing validity extensions. A copy of the order regarding validity extension is attached for reference.

column9: Non reflection of stacks to load into wagons.
column10: A rake was loaded from FSD Kazipet on 10.12.2025. A total 25 stacks were issued out in the said rake. Out of 25 stacks, only 08 stacks were reflecting to load into wagons. A total 17 stacks which in Issue Mode were not reflected to load into the wagons. Due to this the said rake was not able to release. Further, the system is not allowing to mix the varieties in control wagons. As per ICCS circular, the earmarked stacks needs to be weighed 100% on ELWB and the same need to be loaded into the controlled wagons. For example, in a 42 wagon rake, if only two stacks pertain to Boiled Rice-Common and other stacks pertain to Boiled Rice Grade-A, two trucks from the ear marked Common stacks will not fill the entire carrying capacity of the Control Wagon, so it is needed to allow multiple varieties to be loaded into the same control wagon to fill the entire carrying capacity of the wagon. Same will be the situation with respect to multiple crop years. Non reflected stacks are 17B3, 17B12, 17B7, 17C11, 10B2, 3C2, 16B5, 16C8, 16A10, 2A6, 7C9, 6B5, 4C8, 5B4, 1A9, 8A4, 9B12. Hence, kindly resolve the issues to complete the rake.

column10:
When we issue a sample to the Defence RO, defence personnel come and take 12 kg of sample from a particular stack, for example Rice (1A/105). For this transaction, we need to perform an “Other Transaction” outward entry.
In this case, the number of bags is 0, and the quantity is 12 kg. However, in Anna Darpan, the system does not accept 0 bags and shows an error. This issue does not occur in DOS, where a transaction with 0 bags is allowed.
Due to this issue, there is a 12 kg difference between the Anna Darpan stock and the physical stock.

column9: Issue in “View Release Order” – Limited Rows Display, Incorrect Export to PDF & CSV
column10:
1.	CSV Export Limitation
o	The CSV export currently downloads only the rows visible on the screen (maximum 20 rows).
o	If there are large datasets (e.g., 1,000 release orders), the user is forced to export data multiple times (around 50 CSV files), which is highly inefficient.

2.	Limited Rows Display
o	Currently, only a maximum of 20 rows are visible on a single screen/page.
o	When there are hundreds of release orders, navigating page by page becomes extremely cumbersome and time-consuming.
o	This is a major functional drawback in day-to-day operations.
Suggestion:
The system may be enabled to display at least 100 rows per page, with an option for the user to select the number of rows (e.g., 50 / 100 / 200).

3.	PDF Export Issue
o	When exporting the Release Order list to PDF using the Print option, a blank PDF sheet is being generated.
o	This issue requires immediate rectification, as PDF export is essential for official records and reporting.

Expected Behaviour:
CSV export should download the complete release order list, irrespective of the number of rows displayed on the screen.

Impact :
•	Increased manual effort and time consumption
•	Difficulty in handling bulk data
•	Reduced efficiency in official work and reporting

Request

The above issues may kindly be examined and resolved at the earliest to improve usability and operational efficiency of the portal.

column9: Experienced / Inexperienced Bidder Status – Design Limitation
column10:
The portal interface allows a bidder to be marked as Experienced or Inexperienced. However, this status is contract-specific and may vary from one contract to another for the same bidder.

At present, the system treats this attribute as a fixed characteristic of the bidder, which does not provide the required flexibility and may lead to incorrect representation of bidder eligibility across different contracts.

Since Experience/Inexperience status varies from contract to contract, it would be more appropriate to include this field during contract creation, rather than under Add Contractor.

column9: Feedback on inadequacy of Mandtory reports for monitoring and review of essential depot operations
column10:
In the Movement module, there is no provision for generating comprehensive Rake Wise reports for a single depot, multiple depots or all depots attached to a Railhead on date-wise or period-wise basis. Such reports should include details of tagged Railhead, Rake-wise RR number, Commodity-wise and Crop Year-wise dispatch quantity, dispatch station, placement time, release time, total duration for unloading, detention hours and amount, wharfage hours and amount, receipt quantity with bags consumed or saved, and transit loss or gain quantity with percentage. These details are crucial for monitoring rail operations, detention and wharfage liabilities, and overall movement efficiency.

Since all the above data elements are already being captured at various stages by the concerned officials, it is suggested that the System Integrator may comprehensively study the existing IRRS, DOS and the daily, fortnightly and monthly statements prepared at Depot level, as well as the consolidated statements submitted by Divisional Offices to Regional Offices and by Regional Offices to Zonal Offices. Based on this, all essential reports should be systematically provisioned in Anna Darpan so that information can be readily generated, reviewed and utilized optimally at all levels of the organization.

column9: Every time Priority Override Request is arriving
column10:
.Sir,
Please consider the following scenario:
A godown has five (05) stacks with the dates of formation as under:
Stack 1/1 – 01.01.2026
Stack 1/8 – 01.01.2026
Stack 2/6 – 03.01.2026
Stack 2/4 – 04.01.2026
Stack 3/6 – 07.01.2026
The depot has 05 labour gangs, each consisting of 11 labourers, and the depot is required to issue 70 trucks on the same day.
In such circumstances, issuance has to be carried out simultaneously from all five stacks to ease operations and to optimally utilize the available labour gangs. However, the system repeatedly raises a priority override request whenever issuance is attempted from multiple stacks.
Practically, issuing large quantities by completely exhausting one stack before moving to another is not feasible, especially when handling a high number of trucks in a single day. To ensure smooth, efficient, and timely issue operations, issuance from multiple stacks simultaneously becomes unavoidable.
Therefore, it is requested that the system may be suitably modified so that issuance from multiple stacks is allowed without priority override, proportionate to the number of labour gangs available at the depot, to facilitate operational convenience and avoid unnecessary system constraints

To ensure smooth, efficient, and timely issue operations, issuance from multiple stacks simultaneously becomes unavoidable.

column9: Reporting of Issue in Annadarpan During Rake Receipt – Unable to Release Movement at FSD Bommapur-reg.
column10:
As per the subject cited above, it is informed that a rake Ex SHDM to FIH was placed at FCI FSD Bommapur on 17.01.2026. The receipt process was initiated in both DOS and Annadarpan.
In DOS, the rake receipt was recorded shed-wise and released online after matching the ex-wagon issue quantity. The same procedure was followed in Annadarpan by creating movement based on the loading statement, entering rake placement time, and placing the rake. Ex-wagon delivery was successfully issued through Annadarpan.

However, while attempting to online the bags unloaded into the sheds, Annadarpan is showing the same number of bags as loaded in the wagons, but as per unloading records some wagons shown variation of the bags from loading statement. In DOS there is an option for editing the bags as per wagon receipt qty but in AnnaDarpan bags are non editable and must be accounted as per loading details which is creating problem in accounting of the stocks as per unloading details.
In this regard, due to this limitation, we are unable to release the rake movement in Annadarpan & we are accounting the stocks except Ex-Wagon Delivery as per unloading statement through Other Trasanction.

This is for your information and immediate necessary action, please.

column9: Observations and Issues Noticed in Annadarpan System – Request for Resolution
column10:
Sir, This is to bring to your kind notice certain things observed in the Annadarpan system. The details are as under:

1. Killed stacks history is not being displayed for the stacks that were killed in DOS prior to the commencement of work in Annadarpan. This may create difficulties in retrieving stack history in the future whenever required for reference or audit purposes.

2. While proceeding for stack killing, all stacks are being displayed irrespective of whether they are marked for issue or not. Ideally, only sheds under issue mode should be visible in this section.

3. During overriding of stacks, truck-wise entries are routed to the Manager (QC) and Manager (Depot) for approval, and only after approval does the system allow out-weight. This process increases dependency and significantly slows down the operational pace at the depot level. It is therefore requested that overriding permission be enabled on a stack-wise basis instead of truck-wise.

4. In the token list, apart from the token number, other relevant information is concealed. This limits the search functionality and makes it difficult to trace a specific truck when the token number is not available.

5. The weighbridge register is currently missing in the system. Availability of this register is essential to view all truck entries along with other relevant information at a single page and to verify and tally records in case of discrepancies.

In view of the above, we request you to kindly examine these issues and provide an early resolution to ensure smooth and efficient depot operations.

column9: Observations and Issues Noticed in Annadarpan System – Request for Resolution
column10:
Sir, This is to bring to your kind notice certain things observed in the Annadarpan system. The details are as under:

1. Killed stacks history is not being displayed for the stacks that were killed in DOS prior to the commencement of work in Annadarpan. This may create difficulties in retrieving stack history in the future whenever required for reference or audit purposes.

2. While proceeding for stack killing, all stacks are being displayed irrespective of whether they are marked for issue or not. Ideally, only sheds under issue mode should be visible in this section.

3. During overriding of stacks, truck-wise entries are routed to the Manager (QC) and Manager (Depot) for approval, and only after approval does the system allow out-weight. This process increases dependency and significantly slows down the operational pace at the depot level. It is therefore requested that overriding permission be enabled on a stack-wise basis instead of truck-wise.

4. In the token list, apart from the token number, other relevant information is concealed. This limits the search functionality and makes it difficult to trace a specific truck when the token number is not available.

5. The weighbridge register is currently missing in the system. Availability of this register is essential to view all truck entries along with other relevant information at a single page and to verify and tally records in case of discrepancies.

In view of the above, we request you to kindly examine these issues and provide an early resolution to ensure smooth and efficient depot operations.

column9: Provision for all linked depots to receive stocks directly against a single RR number
column10:
During rake unloading at RH SCE (consignee depot FSD Senchowa), RH GUP (consignee depot: HG Balajan), etc the trucks directly dispatched to linked depots are neither weighed at Railhead LWB or at Consignee depot LWB, but are weighed only at the recipient depots due to non-availability of LWB at Railhead and the depots located in different routes. This makes rake unloading online through Annadarpan not possible. 
Hence, there should be provision for all linked depots to receive stocks directly against an RR number (not necessarily through the LWB of the consignee depot alone); However, TL report & DSR for the entire rake/RR should be generated at the consignee depot like FSD Senchowa as per the SOP. Currently, the same is being done in DOS through Offline source by creating multiple identities(Friendly Names) for same rake/RR number which is not advisable and the TL report/DSR for the entire rake/RR are not being generated at the consignee depot.

column9: Discrepancy in Gunny Type Display (SBT 580g) in Annadarpan – Rake EX APCN
column10:
The rake EX APCN, RR No. 262000605 dated 17.01.2026, was placed and unloaded at FSD Coimbatore on 22.01.2026.
For the above rake, inward movement was created in Annadarpan for the two commodities received ie FBRA and FBRC (CY 24–25). In both commodities, the type of gunny was mentioned as SBT (580g) as per the loading statement. The screenshot of the inward movement created is enclosed for your kind reference.
After creation of the inward movement in Annadarpan, the gross weight of the trucks was captured correctly, and the net weight was calculated by the system based on the 580-gram gunny weight. The reference for the net weight calculation can be verified from the test wagon weightment report, which is attached herewith for reference.

For example, if 400 bags are loaded in a truck, the gunny tare is calculated as 0.580 kg × 400 bags, which clearly indicates that the system captures the gunny type as SBT (580g) during net weight calculation. However, in the stack details and movement list, the gunny type is displayed only as “SBT”, without mentioning SBT (580g).
All trucks were weighed, and the weights tallied correctly with the DOS. However, after the release of the rake movement, it was observed that the stack details show the gunny type only as SBT. This was further cross-checked with the movement list, where it is also shown only as SBT.

In view of the above, it is kindly requested to rectify the issue and update the gunny type correctly as SBT (580g) in the system.


The screenshot of the same and test weighment report in Anna darpan is attached for your kind reference.

column9: Regarding creating the IO statement..
column10:
1. IO स्टेटमेंट को क्रिएट करते समय मण्डल कार्यालय धर्मशाला के अंतर्गत आने वाला कोई भी गोदाम, क्रिएट किए जाने वाले IO स्टेटमेंट के किसी भी कॉलम में प्रदर्शित नहीं हो रहा है, जबकि नियमानुसार IO स्टेटमेंट में प्रत्येक गोदाम की अलग-अलग एंट्री किया जाना आवश्यक है।

2. इसके अतिरिक्त, IO स्टेटमेंट में Opening Balance एवं Storage Capacity की जानकारी पूर्व से प्रदर्शित  हो रही है, तथा उक्त प्रविष्टियों को संशोधित (Edit) करने का विकल्प भी उपलब्ध नहीं है।

column9: Priority list mismatch
column10:
With reference to the point stating that ANNA Darpan generates a dynamic priority list based on the latest rules provided by the Quality Division and that the same may differ from DOS, it is respectfully submitted that during scrutiny of the priority list generated in ANNA Darpan, the following anomaly has been observed:

It has been noticed that stacks with an earlier formation date (previous year) are being assigned lower priority, whereas stacks with a later formation date are being given higher priority and are appearing ahead in the priority sequence. This is contrary to the logical expectation wherein older stacks should get priority over newly formed stacks, in line with FIFO principles.
  Further, priority may be generated by combining commodities such as rice under a common category, irrespective of whether they are classified as Common or Grade-A.

column9: Unable to Add Loose Grain via Other Transaction While Closing Release Order – System Constraint
column10:
While closing a release order in Annadarpan, the quantity of loose grain issued from stacks was inadvertently not entered. Due to this, a difference is currently reflected in the closing balance (CB) in Annadarpan.In order to rectify the same, an attempt was made to submit an “Other Transaction” request to incorporate the loose grain quantity. However, the system mandates compulsory entry of bags along with loose grains in the “Other Transaction” module. Since loose grain issue does not involve bags, entry of bags is not applicable. Further, the system does not permit entry of zero bags.Adding bags along with loose grains would adversely affect the total bag position of the depot. As the system does not allow entry of loose grains alone, the correction could not be carried out.In view of the above, it is requested to kindly provide necessary guidance or system-level support to incorporate loose grain quantity without affecting the bag balance, or suggest an alternate procedure to rectify the closing balance difference. column9: In the Annadarpan online portal, during rake loading, day average weight is being adopted instead of stack average weight. This is causing serious discrepancies in stack-wise accounting and disturbing the sanctity of individual miller stacks.
column10:
Present System Problem:

The system is taking the total number of bags weighed during the day.

It calculates the average weight of the 10% weighed bags.

This single day average weight is then applied to all stacks.

Operational Issue:
Each stack belongs to different millers, and each miller delivers stocks with different accepted average weights within the permissible range of 49.750 kg to 50.250 kg.

For example:

Miller A stack average: 49.750 kg

Miller B stack average: 49.950 kg

When the day average is applied across all stacks:

Miller A’s stack (lower average) shows artificial gain.

Miller B’s stack (higher average) shows excess loss.

This disturbs the stack-wise accountability and creates incorrect financial/stock implications.

Technical and Operational Justification:

Each stack is independent and represents stocks from a specific miller.

The average weight should be calculated stack-wise based on the bags weighed from that particular stack.

That stack average weight must be applied only to that stack during loading.

Additional Practical Issue:

When day average weight is applied, the system assumes uniform bag count per wagon, since wagon carrying capacity remains constant.

However, in actual operations, different stacks have different average weights, resulting in different number of bags per wagon.

Therefore, loading is practically done based on stack average weight, not day average.

It is requested that the Annadarpan system be modified so that:

Stack-wise average weight is calculated based on the bags weighed from each stack.

The respective stack average weight is applied during rake loading.

Day average weight should not be applied across all stacks.

This change is essential to:

Maintain stack-wise sanctity.

Ensure correct accounting of gains and losses.

Reflect actual field loading practices.

column9: Gunny Account
column10: At FSD Olavakkode, there are 31 sheds constituting 5 units, and the gunny stock is presently maintained unit-wise in the manual registers. However, in the Annadarpan module, gunny stock is reflected shed-wise. While attempting to issue gunny from a particular shed, the system permits the transaction only if sufficient balance is available in that specific shed in the module. Even though adequate stock may be available within the same unit, the issue cannot be processed unless the balance is shown in that particular shed in Annadarpan. This practice is leading to discrepancies between the gunny account maintained in the manual registers on a unit-wise basis and the shed-wise balance available in the Annadarpan system.

Hence if Handling & Transport both are selected as Type of contractor, the name of contractor should be visible in all three types of contractors list i.e. Transport, Handling, H&T.  Please do needful in this regard.

column9: Evening stock position not showing non issueable stock
column10:
The evening stock position report is a vital report for daily transaction information
 If a stack is marked as non issueable then the closing balance is not showing the quantity and generating report of closing balance by reducing the bag and quantity of the non issueable stack
Sometimes non issueable is marked by mistake due to typo error. So the CB must not be generated without taking its quantity into calculation.

column9: All Stack pertaining to FRK and NON-FRK are not visible during loading in same special at Siding Godown
column10:
Sir,
While implementing the Annadarpan some of the issue facing during transaction, due to which we are restrict to implement the Annadarpan in full fledged manner. Some of the issues we are trying to describe in detail to explain the problem.
As you are aware, the data that was migrated to Annadarpan from the Depot Online system consisted entirely of Raw Rice Common or Boiled Rice Common varieties. Since the Depot Online system does not support FRK varieties, all stacks are taken either as Raw Rice Common or Boiled Rice Common in the Depot Online system. DOS does not have the provision for FRK. However, in the rake to be loaded, some of the stacks in the Rake were old stacks that had been migrated from DOS, and some stacks were new, which were received through Annadarpan and then taken as CMR. Since FCB is a siding godown where at least 10% of the quantity of all stacks loaded from the siding is to be weighed on a truck through a weighbridge, the average weight per bag applies uniformly to all stacks loaded from the siding. For this, all trucks loading from the siding need to be in the same special; only then will the average weight per bag be correct. The new FRK stacks that were taken in Annadarpan are not showing up in the common Rice movement during rake loading. Further CMR cannot be received in all those stacks until all of the stack to be issued in DOS are also issued in Annadarpan and killed, because those stacks do not appear during CMR receipt as Vacant Stack.
Kindly rectify the problem as soon as possible.

column9: Feedback on inadequacy of Mandtory reports for monitoring and review of essential depot operations
column10:
In the Sales module, there is no provision for generating Commodity-wise, Scheme-wise and Crop Year-wise Allocation and Offtake statements for a single depot, multiple depots or all depots under a Divisional Office, Regional Office or Zonal Office for a specific date, multiple dates, a date range or month. column9: Regarding Contractor Details to ADD Contractor
column10:
Kindly refer to the screenshot. While adding a contractor in the Anna Darpan Portal, the following interface-related issues have been observed:

1. MSE Contractor Classification

The interface provides a mandatory field titled “Is MSE Contractor.”

At present, there is no option to indicate that a contractor is non-MSE, which makes it impossible to proceed in such cases.

Further, if a contractor belongs to the MSE category and simultaneously falls under General / OBC or other categories (other than SC, ST, Women Enterprise), there is no appropriate option available in the interface to capture this combination.

2. Experienced / Inexperienced Bidder Status

The interface allows selection of a bidder as Experienced or Inexperienced.

However, this status is contract-specific and may vary from one contract to another for the same bidder.

The current design treats this as a fixed attribute of the bidder, which does not provide the required flexibility.

column9: Incorrect ALP Dosage and Consumption Calculation in Curative Treatment - Reg
column10:
While recording Curative treatment under the Preservation module, it is noticed that required quantity of ALP is being calculated incorrectly. This is mainly due to wrong provision of standard dosage of chemical, which is currently set as 9Units/Mt of food grains instead of 3Units/Mt of foodgrains. For better clarity, the actual dosage of ALP consumption may be shown as two different types as follows:
1. 9 Gram (Each tablet is 3 Gram) / Mt of food grains - For a stack weighing 196.094 Mt the required quantity of ALP works out to 1.764 Kg  (i.e., 1764 grams)
2. 3Units/Mt of foodgrains - For the same stack the quantity of chemical needed in units is 588 Units.

However, for the same stack in Anna Darpan the quantity of chemical used is shown as 1764.8440704 (Screenshot of Annadarpan and DOS is attached) which reflects the calculation in grams, whereas the chemical stock is maintained in Units (Tablets). Since the chemical stock is managed based on units, the consumption also shall be calculated in units.

column9: Alignment of RO Numbering Pattern in Anna Darpan
column10:
Release Order number presently being generated in Anna Darpan is in the format “ED12029/12-2025/PRC-007”, whereas the corresponding Release Order number generated in DOS follows the format “ED/12/PHH/Boiled Rice-7191”. It is respectfully pointed out that the numbering pattern in DOS clearly reflects the concerned scheme and commodity, which facilitates easy identification, segregation, verification, reconciliation, reporting, and audit scrutiny during day-to-day operations.

However, the current Release Order numbering format being generated in Anna Darpan does not indicate the scheme, due to which scheme-wise identification of Release Orders is not possible from the RO number itself, resulting in avoidable operational inconvenience and increased dependence on manual cross-verification.

In this regard, it is suggested that the Release Order numbering pattern in Anna Darpan may be rationalised and aligned with operational requirements by adopting a standardized and scheme-indicative format incorporating Depot Code, short form of Scheme Name, Allocation Month, short form of Commodity, and a three- or four-digit running sequence number viz ED12029/12-2025/PHH/PRC-007 . Adoption of such a self-explanatory numbering logic would ensure uniformity, operational clarity, continuity with existing practices, and ease of monitoring, reporting, reconciliation, and audit verification.

In this regard, it is suggested that the Release Order numbering pattern in Anna Darpan may be rationalised and aligned with operational requirements by adopting a standardized and scheme-indicative format incorporating Depot Code, short form of Scheme Name, Allocation Month, short form of Commodity, and a three- or four-digit running sequence number viz ED12029/12-2025/PHH/PRC-007 . Adoption of such a self-explanatory numbering logic would ensure uniformity, operational clarity, continuity with existing practices, and ease of monitoring, reporting, reconciliation, and audit verification.

column9: Proposal for System Enhancement in Anna Darpan – Stack-Level Priority Override During Rake Loading Operations
column10:
It is submitted for kind consideration that a practical operational difficulty is being faced in Anna Darpan during rake loading operations at depot level.

During rake operations, loading is carried out in a time-bound manner with 10–12 stacks operating simultaneously, involving approximately 120–150 trucks within limited railway free time. At present, whenever a truck is loaded from a non-priority stack, the system generates a “Priority Overriding” pop-up, and after submission, the transaction requires multi-level approvals from:

Manager (QC)

Manager (D)

Divisional Manager (within the same crop year)

In large-scale rake loading scenarios, obtaining approval for each individual truck becomes operationally impractical and causes delay in truck loading and out-weighment. This is particularly challenging when:

Stacks are temporarily marked non-priority due to infestation or lab analysis.

Simultaneous loading is undertaken from multiple stacks (10–12 stacks).

Since priority is inherently linked to stack status and not to individual trucks, the requirement of truck-wise approval creates avoidable administrative burden and hampers time-bound rake operations.

Proposal for Enhancement:
It is proposed that the system may be modified to allow priority override approval at stack level instead of truck-wise approval. Once approved for a specific stack, loading from that stack during the rake operation may proceed without repeated approvals for each truck.

Such modification will:

Improve operational efficiency during rake loading

Reduce approval delays

Align system workflow with field-level operational practices

Ensure compliance while maintaining accountability

The matter may kindly be examined, and necessary enhancement in the concerned sub-module of Anna Darpan may be considered at the earliest.

Submitted for kind consideration and necessary action.

column9: Incorrect Receipt and Issue Entries Reflected in Killed Stack History Report
column10:
Sir,
With reference to the subject cited above, it is submitted that an issue has been observed in the Killed Stack History Report generated through Anna Darpan.

It has been noticed that the Killed Stack History Report is still capturing certain receipt and issue entries, despite the fact that no such receipt or issue transactions have been carried out for the concerned killed stacks. The appearance of these entries is inconsistent with the actual operational records maintained in DOS and physical registers.

Such incorrect reflection of transactions raises serious concerns regarding the correctness and reliability of historical transaction mapping in the system. If not rectified, this anomaly may adversely affect reconciliation of records, audit verification, and the overall integrity of stock history data.

For your kind information and perusal, the relevant Killed Stack History Report has been attached herewith.

It is therefore requested that the above issue may kindly be examined and rectified at the earliest to ensure accuracy of historical data and transparency in reporting.

column9: Priority Override Approval in Anna Darpan
column10:
In Anna Darpan portal, whenever a stack is being marked for issue and then Shed In-charge is proceeding with loading of bags from that particular stack, priority override request is being generated (from SHED IN_CHARGE ID) for each truck loaded from that particular stack. The priority override request is then forwarded to MANAGER_QC ID, who in return has to forward the same to MANAGER_DEPOT ID for the final approval. This entire procedure has to be repeated for each truck loaded from stacks that have been marked to issue on any particular day. This is unnecessarily delaying the delivery operation in the depot and hampering weighment of loaded trucks smoothly.

Since priority is overridden stack-wise and not truck-wise, it will be relevant if priority override request is generated only once for a single stack from the SHED IN_CHARGE ID, forwarded to MANAGER_QC ID, who further forwards the same to MANAGER_DEPOT ID for the final approval.

Ticket was already raised regarding this matter on 02.02.2026, however, the issue still remains unresolved making it difficult to update the contract details on the portal

column9: Issue Regarding Weight Capturing and Token Generation for Truck Dispatch from Rail Head Bairabi
column10:
It is to inform that at FSD Bairabi, trucks are being dispatched to other depots directly from Rail Head Bairabi where a rake is placed.

In the existing process, trucks first report at FSD Bairabi for in-weight. Thereafter, the said trucks are loaded from a particular wagon at Rail Head Bairabi and again report at FSD Bairabi for out-weight before being dispatched to the respective depots. The weight capturing is presently being done through Leotronics, as the weight capturing facility is not available in DOS.

Token creation for such movements is being carried out using the option “Direct Movement from Rail Head” under the “Movement by Rail Inward” module. However, it has been observed in Anna Darpan that there is no provision for weight capturing for trucks being dispatched to other depots from the Rail Head.

At present, there is only a single page available through which tokens are generated, wherein tare weight and gross weight have to be entered manually. Further, it is observed that in such cases, generation of Truck Chit is not possible through the system, and the depot staff are compelled to issue manual RMP (Road Movement Permit).

The above limitations may kindly be examined and necessary system provisions may be made to facilitate proper weight capturing and document generation for such movements.
